edits.why: Shrink the whole figure about 7% to match the reference height from crest to feet
Keep the vertical centring after zooming out, since the reference feet sit slightly higher in frame

hist.diagnosis: The model reads about 7–8% too large in frame: the crest sits higher, the feet sit lower, and red outlines the right arm, the legs and the top of the shield, so the overall scale is off before any local mismatch. The shield also looks too tall and too edge-on compared with the reference, but scale comes first, so this round only pulls the camera back.

edits.why: Turn the shield further toward edge-on so its projected width shrinks to match the reference's narrow oval
The reference shield runs from about chest height to just below the knee, so it is shorter than the current one
Slightly narrower, to remove the red band past its right edge
Move it slightly out from the body and down, so it stops covering the torso and its top drops to chest height

hist.diagnosis: The biggest mismatch is the shield. In the reference it is turned further toward edge-on, so it looks narrow and sits mostly to the right of the torso, with its top at about chest height. In the render it is wide and nearly face-on, covers the figure's left chest and rises higher, which leaves large red areas on its left and right edges and above it. The pose, facing direction and camera are otherwise close, so this round only changes the shield.

edits.why: Turn the whole figure further toward image-left to match the reference three-quarter facing. This moves the left shoulder and shield back and in, which narrows the shield's projection and the shoulder span.
Small nudge to keep the feet and torso centred, since turning shifts the shield mass inward.

hist.diagnosis: The reference figure stands in a clear three-quarter view, turned toward image-left: we see the sash side of the torso, the left shoulder and the shield fall away from the camera, and the shield shows up as a narrow, nearly edge-on oval. The render is almost frontal, which accounts for the red on the shield's right edge, the extra-wide shoulders, and the crest reading as a flat vertical spike instead of a front-to-back fan. Shrinking the shield last round was rejected, so the extra width likely comes from the body's turn rather than the shield's size.

edits.why: More facet jitter, to give the dense small folded facets seen across the reference's torso, skirt and legs
A smaller key light gives harder light-to-shadow transitions between facets, which should raise the facet-edge correlation
The reference's lit faces are near white and the render's are dull grey, so brighten the key to restore that contrast
Slightly less roughness lets facets catch distinct highlights, as in the reference, instead of flat diffuse grey

hist.diagnosis: The silhouette and pose are close, and the edge term (0.94 × 0.2 ≈ 0.19) is now the largest weighted loss. The reference is covered in crisp, high-contrast crumpled-paper facets under a hard bright key, while the render is soft, hazy and dim, so its facet edges barely register. Rounds 2 and 3 changed the shield geometry and the figure's yaw and were both rejected, so this round leaves geometry alone and only sharpens the facets and lighting.

edits.why: Pull the right shoulder in and slightly down to remove the red band outside the shoulder cap and bring it level with the left shoulder, as in the reference
Bring the upper arm closer to the torso, because the reference upper arm hangs near the body
Angle the forearm outward to fill the blue gap along the outer forearm
Move the fist out from the thigh, matching the reference's open gap between hand and leg

hist.diagnosis: The global read is close: same three-quarter facing, the camera slightly above, and the key light from image-right. The clearest remaining shape error is the figure's right arm (image-left). The render's shoulder and upper arm stick out too far (red band outside the shoulder and upper arm), while the reference's forearm and fist angle outward away from the thigh (blue along the outer forearm and hand). Shield and yaw edits were rejected in earlier rounds, so this round works only on the right-arm joint chain.

edits.why: Swing the elbow outward to fill the blue band on the outer upper arm and open a gap to the torso
Move the forearm outward and slightly up, to remove the red against the hip and fill the blue on the outer forearm
Move the fist out and up to match the reference hand position and remove the red below it

hist.diagnosis: The figure faces the right way, and the camera and lighting read correctly. The biggest remaining error is the right arm (image left): there is blue along its outer edge and red along its inner edge from elbow to fist, so the reference arm hangs further from the torso with an open gap at the waist. There is also a small red overhang below the fist.
